<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 40:15">Targ. O. Gen. XL, 15</cite> <he>גְּנֵיבְנָא</he> ed. Berl. I have been stolen.—Ruth R. introd. 3 (a trial before a Roman court) <he>גְּנַבְתּוּן לא גְנַבְנוּן</he> “Ye have stolen”.—‘We have not’ …; <he>לא גָנַבְתְּ מאן ג׳ עמך</he> “thou hast not stolen? Who has been stealing with thee?”; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 37:2">Gen. R. s. 37</cite>; s. 63.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 65b:15">B. Kam. 65ᵇ</cite> <he>תורא גַנְבִי מינך</he> was it an ox I stole from thee?—
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 67b:14">Ib. 67ᵇ</cite> <he>עד דגְנֵיב תרי</he> (he is not bound to pay) unless he stole two animals; a. fr.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 23:30">Targ. Jer. XXIII, 30</cite>.—2) <cite ref="C01078">same</cite>.

Keth. 19ᵃ גַנּוֹבָא גַּנּוּבֵי למה לך וכ׳ O thou cunning man, what is the use of thy going round about?; Yeb. 91ᵃ; B. Bath. 133ᵃ גַּנָּבָא גנובי Ms. R. (ed. גנבא גנבי, corr. acc.).—Part. pass. מְגַנַּב crooked.
